body:
Conclusion: the observation-cursor behaviour that applies to this workspace's integration is the pinned Ordarium contract's — a single GLOBAL, filter-independent durable position. The "per-subscription" reading in docs/engineering/notes/cursor-note.md is a stale informational record and does not govern.

Why (applying docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md):

1. Rule 1 = the published contract of the exact pinned version. The pin is @ordarium/* 1.3.1 (package.json lines 32–37; pnpm-workspace.yaml lines 15–18; installed node_modules/@ordarium/core/package.json and @ordarium/ledger-sqlite/package.json both report 1.3.1). That pin, not the 1.2.0 figures recorded in docs/engineering/07 (r19), is the exact pinned version.

2. That contract states global/filter-independent:
   - node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts — StateChangePage.cursor: "Opaque, filter-independent durable position of the last delivered change." StateChangeFilter.namespace: "Restrict observation to one namespace; absent observes every namespace" (the filter narrows which changes are returned; it does not partition the cursor). StateChangeFeed.changes(filter?, cursor?).
   - node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js changes(): semantic validation compares `after` against `#stateChangeHighWater()` with the explicit comment "the cursor is a global, filter-independent position, so this compares against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace's last sequence" (ORD-BOOT-0.1: only the whole-ledger mark can move the cursor; a restored/replaced ledger lowers it and fails closed with InvalidCursorError). The returned cursor is encoded from the ledger-wide change_seq of the last delivered row, and compareAndSetState inserts exactly one ordering row per committed revision (ORD-BOOT-0), so a committed revision and its observable position are never split.

3. Rule 3 (informational records) cannot override rule 1, and the note disqualifies itself twice: it is marked "informational, not normative" and admits it "was not updated against the current pinned artifact". A repo-wide literal search finds "per-subscription" nowhere else and "global" in no other cursor context — the note is the sole, explanatory source. It also describes an "earlier Ordarium line", i.e. it predates the current 1.3.1 pin.

4. No normative project source (PLMP-SDS, docs/engineering/03) claims otherwise for this Ordarium interface. Palimpsest's own cursor concepts (graph.project.cursor = canonical event position; viewCursor = view-freshness validator, spec 35) are a different, project-internal surface and are not in conflict.

Consequences for the integration: a cursor returned by StateChangeFeed.changes() under a namespace filter is valid ledger-wide and may be reused with a different or absent namespace filter without losing position; no per-namespace/per-subscription cursor bookkeeping is required or meaningful; and a cursor above the ledger's global high-water mark (restored/replaced database) fails closed. Scope note: Palimpsest's telemetry load path today consumes store.list()'s nextCursor (keyset pagination), which is a distinct surface; the repo contains no call to changes()/stateChangeFeed, so this resolution binds the feed's semantics without implying a code change.
